extracted.intended_audience: late-night TV writers, comedy writers, and comedians producing topical jokes
extracted.subtask_short: writing topical jokes for late-night TV
extracted.subtask_description: Practical notes and a working rubric for producing daily, topical jokes for a TV host: pitch many options, iterate rapidly, prioritize host-appropriate, perishable material that lands on first read. Emphasizes workflow timing, culling rates, and clear anti-patterns to avoid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily-Joke Workflow (timeline and expectations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The day is structured: 9 a.m. scan news; 10 a.m. pitch 10 jokes per topic; 11 a.m. writer's room kills/refines/selects; 1 p.m. rewrite survivors with the host's voice; 4 p.m. rehearsal cuts another 30%; 11:35 p.m. live, and 80% of what you wrote is gone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitch high volume (10 per topic) knowing most will die; expect multiple rounds of culling and rewriting; plan for major attrition by rehearsal and live performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific-to-TODAY / perishable jokes
rubrics_metrics.description: Jokes that are specific to TODAY (perishable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness is valuable in daily TV; highly topical items survive the rewrite process but may not be desirable if they remain funny tomorrow (see working rubric item about being funny tomorrow).

rubrics_metrics.name: Host-persona compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Jokes that work with the host's persona (not yours).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write so the host can deliver without losing their established voice; prioritize material that feels natural for the host rather than the writer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Landing on the first read
rubrics_metrics.description: Jokes whose structure is clean enough to land on the first read aloud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a joke doesn't land the first time it's read aloud, it likely won't survive rehearsal or live performance; favor clear setups and immediate payoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requires existing setup from host
rubrics_metrics.description: Jokes that don't require setup the host hasn't already given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid material that depends on new exposition the host hasn't provided; rely on what the audience already knows or what the host will naturally establish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hard No — explaining a Wikipedia article
rubrics_metrics.description: Anything that requires explaining a Wikipedia article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid jokes that depend on lengthy factual explanation or background-teaching; these are inappropriate for rapid late-night formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hard No — punching at unknown targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Anything that punches at someone the audience hasn't been introduced to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't target people or entities the audience doesn't recognize; jokes need shared referents to land quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hard No — 'this happened' without a comedic angle
rubrics_metrics.description: Anything where the joke is "this happened" without a comedic angle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merely reporting an event isn't a joke; ensure there's an angle, twist, or interpretive comedic frame.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hard No — ages poorly within 24 hours
rubrics_metrics.description: Anything that ages poorly within 24 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extremely perishable material can be worthless after a day; balance immediacy with usable shelf-life depending on goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comic-book principle — panel as punchline
rubrics_metrics.description: A panel is a punchline; the page is the setup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use spatial and sequential structure (in comics or analogous joke structure) to set up and deliver a concentrated payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comic-book principle — smallest panel for the funniest moment
rubrics_metrics.description: The funniest moment is usually the smallest panel, where the reader's eye is forced to slow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing and rhythm can be manipulated by size/pace; in spoken jokes, use brevity and a micro-moment to force attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comic-book principle — lettering rhythm as timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Lettering rhythm (line breaks within a balloon) is comic timing on the page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Micro-level lineation and breaks affect timing; in scriptwriting, pay attention to pause and cadence equivalent to line breaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kibblesmith Rubric — is it specific to a real, current event?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the joke specific to a real, current event?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topical specificity is a criterion — confirm the joke ties clearly to a real, timely item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kibblesmith Rubric — could the host say it?
rubrics_metrics.description: Could the host say it without losing their persona?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test each line for host-voice fit; if delivery would feel off for the host, discard or rewrite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kibblesmith Rubric — does it land on first read?
rubrics_metrics.description: Does it land on the first read aloud?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate readability and instant payoff are critical in the writing room and on air.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kibblesmith Rubric — is it cleaner than the previous joke?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is it cleaner than the joke before it in the script?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparative cleanliness matters; prefer a tighter, clearer version over a clunkier alternative in the lineup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kibblesmith Rubric — will it still be funny tomorrow morning?
rubrics_metrics.description: Will it still be funny tomorrow morning? (If yes — it might not be timely enough.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as a diagnostic for timeliness: enduring jokes may be insufficiently topical for nightly formats; conversely, extremely ephemeral jokes may also be risky.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kibblesmith Rubric — have you written nine others?
rubrics_metrics.description: Have you written nine others to compete with this one?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generate volume (at least ten options) so the strongest lines can be chosen; treat each candidate as competing within a set.
